anomalies.observed: On the Microcontroller sheet the USB-C receptacle VBUS pin (J13 A4) is drawn on a single node that carries BOTH the '+5V' power symbol and the 'VBUS' net label. On the Power sheet the TPS2121 mux U10 has IN2 (pin 2) on the '+5V' net and OUT (pin 1) on the 'VBUS' net, and the buck U2 input (pin 3) is also on 'VBUS'. Because the USB VBUS pin ties '+5V' and 'VBUS' together, the mux's IN2 and its OUT (and hence the buck input and the 12 V rail through the mux) are shorted.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification the USB VBUS pin must feed the '+5V' net only (J12 VBUS pins -> +5V net -> U5 IN2), and the mux OUT must be a separate internal 'VBUS' rail that is 'distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux'. The two nets must not be joined; the mux is what arbitrates between them.

power.kicad_sch, U10 TPS2121RUXR: IN2 (pin 2) = '+5V', OUT (pin 1) = 'VBUS' (TP3); U2 AP63203WU IN (pin 3) = 'VBUS'

J12 ... VBUS pins (A4/A9/B4/B9) -> +5V net -> U5 pin 2/2_1 (IN2). ... outputs a single OUT ... onto the VBUS net ... note this net is named VBUS in the netlist but is distinct from the USB +5V net upstream of the mux

anomalies.impact: The power-mux arbitration is defeated: '+5V' and the internal 'VBUS' rail are merged. When the 12 V barrel jack is connected, the raw 12 V appears on the mux OUT and is shorted onto the '+5V' net, i.e. back-fed onto the USB-C VBUS pin (potentially damaging the host), and the mux's current limit / seamless switchover no longer controls the USB path.
